acceptance_criteria: Sequencing and scope: no dispatch gate applies and this goal has no dependency. It converts nothing E6 converts and adds no non-test executable (user decision 2026-10-07: everything new is TypeScript); the three skills are Markdown procedures and the new test is plain bash. It does edit .ai/ci/local-ci.json (only the existing tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py sources hash value), so E6's e6-sk-00-ledger waits for this goal's merge, as does every other E6 goal that edits that file (all eight at #120 head a514f182); E6's py-lib goal (tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py), v1-port goal (tests/xskp_p5_readiness_policy_test.sh, tests/ach_s01_readiness_policy_test.sh, which it ports in the narrowed form of the retained-policy criterion) and test-harness goal (tests/catalog_contract_test.sh) also wait for it. XSKP-P5-02 (#118) shares .ai/skills/catalog-audit.json, .ai/ci/local-ci.json and tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py and serializes with this goal in either order. Never two open PRs on one shared file; the later PR rebases on the earlier. The E6 waits are one-way, so there is no cycle. Any change outside this scope, including tests/fixtures/host-default-golden.json, any other .ai/ci/local-ci.json value or the retained policy JSON files, requires a reviewed scope successor before it is made.

Three role skills, evolution-rollout, wiki-maintainer and skill-proposer, exist under 02-govern-plan/ with catalog.json entries: owner_phase 02-govern-plan, lifecycle experimental and supported_hosts [] (coordinator decision 2026-10-08, the pre-G-03 edit-article precedent), until ai-catapult's tswc-ac-b1 evolve/ layout and tswc-ac-b3 validation CLI land. The entries stay catalogued for docs, the validator and lifecycle but resolve into no host bundle: ai-catapult's src/skill-resolver.js:122-128 bundles every non-deprecated entry whose supported_hosts names the host, so the empty list is what keeps a skills.lock bump from shipping them. scripts/catalog.py accepts the empty list (its lines 56-60), and the catalog validator passes. python3 scripts/catalog-query.py lists none of the three for any host, even with --include-lifecycle experimental, and --skill <name> exits 2 for each of them on every host. Default installs, the default catalog view and tests/fixtures/host-default-golden.json stay unchanged: bash tests/host_default_golden_test.sh, bash tests/lifecycle_installers_test.sh and bash tests/install_cross_host_parity_test.sh pass without edits. Promotion (listing hosts) belongs to the successor plan or a later goal.

Generated surfaces are regenerated in the same change set: README.md, AGENTS.md, 01-discover-decide/ask-ai-catapult/CATALOG.md and 02-govern-plan/README.md with the catalog doc generator (python3 scripts/generate-skill-docs.py, or its form on main at implementation), and .ai/skills/catalog-audit.json and .ai/skills/modernization-report.md with the catalog validator's --write-audit mode. The generator's --check mode, the validator, bash tests/skill-catalog_test.sh and bash tests/agents_index_test.sh pass.

The role bodies follow the repo conventions: description at most 160 characters and SKILL.md body at most 100 lines with no new description or body-line exception entry, Quick Start first, progressive disclosure, CONTEXT.md vocabulary, and Codex/OpenCode parity (bash tests/codex_parity_test.sh and bash tests/opencode_parity_test.sh pass).

The role bodies speak B1's evolve/ vocabulary exactly as master intake sections 5.4 and 6-B1 state: raw/<run-id>/ write-once traces, wiki/ with append-only logs.md and skill-impact.md, proposals/ overlays, PURPOSE.md, the audit-entry schema and the judgment-record schema (judgment_id, run_id, candidate_overlay_sha256, skill_under_test, task_set_id, task_set_version, judge_model, rubric_sha256, per_criterion_scores[], weighted_aggregate, verdict, cost_usd, recorded_at, recorder). The proposer is atomic single-skill, the wiki stays append-only even on reject, and in-place skill mutation is forbidden (section 3c). The cross-lane edge to tswc-ac-b1 is non-blocking, and a vocabulary-sync note is recorded for when B1 lands.

Blindness is enforced by the environment, never by a prompt check (master F3, section 6-B2): the evolution-rollout procedure builds a wiki-stripped export with path denial (no evolve/ and no git history, so wiki files are unreachable, including through history), and its SKILL.md carries the export commands in exactly one fenced block with the info string bash blindness-sandbox. Every record states that the prompt-grep gate is a cheap pre-check only.

Red leg (section 4.7): the new tests/blindness_sandbox_test.sh is plain bash with no embedded Python or other interpreter program. It extracts the bash blindness-sandbox block from the evolution-rollout SKILL.md and runs exactly those commands against a seeded source repository in a cleanup-bound temporary directory, so the test and the procedure cannot drift. It proves the workload is exported while a direct read of evolve/wiki/ and a read through git history both fail; it is red when the block is missing; and its negative fixtures (the extracted block with path denial removed, and a history-preserving export) are red. It is discovered by tests/test-scripts.sh and reports a nonzero Results: PASS count.

The roles carry the locked loop economics: the $100 per cycle ceiling (user 2026-10-04; section 5.5 pre-reject before spend plus gate accounting), human out-of-band judges (section 4.4), and no citation of the WikiSkill paper for any threshold value (section 3a).

Retained-policy narrowing (coordinator decision 2026-10-08): tests/xskp_p5_readiness_policy_test.sh and tests/ach_s01_readiness_policy_test.sh keep asserting that .ai/handoff/xskp-p5-readiness-policy.retained.json and .ai/handoff/ach-skills-contract-v2/s01-readiness-policy-v1.retained.json equal their pinned digests, unchanged. Retained snapshots are historical evidence, not live claims: each 'every source digest is current' assertion becomes a well-formedness assertion over the retained source digests, and each contract-acceptance simulation relaxes only source-digest currency for the retained policy's own source entries, exactly as it already relaxes repository-root equality. Every other assertion and expected gap stays unchanged, and the retained JSON files are never edited. Both review lanes record explicit acceptance of this narrowing before merge.

tests/catalog_contract_test.sh no longer hard-codes the default count (-eq 36). The literal is replaced in plain bash: the codex default view must be nonempty and name each skill once. The existing per-host assertion that each default view equals catalog.json's stable/compatibility membership stays, so together they fix the count from data, as tests/skill-catalog_test.sh already derives its count. With supported_hosts [] the codex default view stays 36, so this change keeps promotion from editing the test again. No other assertion is weakened.

SKILL.md no-growth guard: the ACH-S-05 assertion at tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py:661-664 (git diff --exit-code 977ed13b6f091a279828e1ddb4665df0a17b52ea -- '*/SKILL.md') fails once the three new SKILL.md files are committed, and with it bash tests/run-tests.sh. It is re-pinned in #118's digest form (#118 at 9299b7c, tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py:661-682): sha256 over every tracked */SKILL.md path, index mode and working-tree bytes, sorted. If #118 has merged, this goal advances that digest; otherwise it introduces the form and #118 advances it. The re-pin covers exactly the deliberate addition of the three role SKILL.md files, and every other assertion in the test is unchanged. .ai/ci/local-ci.json changes only the existing tests/readiness_v2_migrate_test.py sources hash value: no other key, value, command, workflow, tier or format changes.
